thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate detected on inference-redwood-runtime-prod (model: rdlw-7b-q8). 5xx spike (segfaults/OOM) crossed threshold 5m ago. Error rate 18% on /v1/generate. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/xyz/runtime-5xx

marie (oncall): ack — paging SRE and runtime eng. I'm grabbing the keyboard.

marie (oncall): quick question — which customers/routes impacted most? any correlation with batch size or sequence length?

ai-runtime-eng: we're seeing repeated segfaults in the runtime worker process (libjemalloc region) during kv-cache writes for long sequences. Sample log snippets:
```
[2026-03-14T09:11:03Z] worker-12 PID 2345 SIGSEGV at 0x7f8c... while writing 8192 bytes to kv_cache
Backtrace:
#0 0x7f8c2b4a in memcpy
#1 0x55a1b0 runtime::kv_write
#2 0x55a1d2 serve::step
#3 0x55a3f0 request_handler
```
Core dumps present on 3 nodes (gce-prod-gpu-1..3).

dylan: good context. marie — run mitigation steps below and keep updating. I'll loop in SRE lead.

marie (oncall): executing mitigations now: 1) disable batching on the affected model variant, 2) route 60% traffic to fallback model (rdlw-7b-std) with conservative memory settings, 3) restart affected pods one-by-one. Posting commands.

marie (oncall): disable batching (temporary):
```
# update route config
curl -X POST "https://controlplane/api/routes/rdlw-7b-q8/patch" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"batching": {"enabled": false}}'
```

marie (oncall): route change (50->60% to fallback):
```
# flip routing policy
kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: redwood/v1
kind: TrafficSplit
metadata:
  name: rdlw-7b-split
  namespace: prod
spec:
  primary:
    model: rdlw-7b-q8
    weight: 40
  fallback:
    model: rdlw-7b-std
    weight: 60
EOF
```

ops-bot: :white_check_mark: Route change accepted; rollout id=roll-20260314-001.

ai-runtime-eng: immediate note — disabling batching should reduce concurrent memory pressure. Also set max_batch_tokens=512 and max_concurrency=2 for the q8 variant while we investigate. Example patch below:
```
# patch config
kubectl patch cm runtime-config -n prod --type merge -p '{"data":{"rdlw-7b-q8.max_batch_tokens":"512","rdlw-7b-q8.max_concurrency":"2"}}'
```

sre-lead: I'm watching node metrics. OOM events stopped on node gce-prod-gpu-2 after restart, but worker segfaults still visible on -1 and -3. Logging shows slightly different mem footprints per request.

ai-runtime-eng: we pulled a few core dumps. Repro locally with a long prompt + streaming enabled reproduces same crash in allocator region. Likely regression from the allocator change in runtime v1.14. Rolling back that patch is high-risk; prefer temporary traffic routing + disable batching while we root cause.

marie (oncall): current customer impact: ~12 active customers saw 5xx; top two (acme-analytics, chatly) experienced degraded availability on /v1/generate for ~18 minutes. We're notifying CS. Error rate down from 18% -> 3% after routing to fallback and restart of 2 nodes.

customer-success: notified acme-analytics and chatly (incident notice sent). Both opted for continued traffic to fallback model; they've acknowledged. Preparing post-incident customer summary.

dylan: ok tactical plan for next 60m: 1) keep batching disabled on q8 variant, 2) keep traffic split (40/60), 3) collect sampled failing payloads and core dumps, 4) SRE to keep pods on restart loop until no segfaults for 15m, 5) runtime-eng to reproduce and if necessary revert allocator change in a canary patch.

ai-runtime-eng: reproduction notes posted to the incident doc (link): https://docs.redwood.company/incident/1768009987. Short-term hotfix candidate: guard around kv_cache write to validate sizes before memcpy (low-risk guard). We'll prepare a canary build and push to canary pool.

marie (oncall): performing controlled canary restart with patched build on one node. Command:
```
# canary deploy patched runtime
kubectl set image deployment/runtime-worker runtime=registry.redwood/patched-runtime:v1.14.1-canary -n prod
```

ops-bot: :information_source: Canary deployment started (canary-pool-1). Monitoring logs.

sre-lead: metrics: after routing + config change, 5xx dropped to 2.7% cluster-wide, latency slightly up (~90ms) but within SLO. No customer escalations beyond initial notices.

ai-runtime-eng: canary looks good for 20m — no segfaults on the canary node. We'll promote patch to 20% gradually while keeping routing policy. Patch includes bounds check at kv_write and additional null checks.

dylan: if canary remains clean for 30m, start 20% promotion and notify CS. Keep batching disabled until we confirm stability under load.

marie (oncall): handing off to dylan — I'm on-call for another 25m but need to step into a meeting. Handoff notes:
- mitigations applied (batching disabled, traffic split, config patched)
- canary running: id canary-20260314-01
- customer impact: 2 customers notified, error rate dropped to ~3%

marie (oncall): @dylan, take over to watch promotion; escalate to Eng Director if canary fails.

dylan: taking over. Thanks marie — will keep this thread updated and post timeline for postmortem.

customer-success: we will send a follow-up with root-cause summary after postmortem.

ai-runtime-eng: follow-ups we will own: 1) postmortem with root cause and timeline, 2) revert or harden allocator change depending on deeper analysis, 3) test coverage to include long-sequence kv-write scenarios, 4) add a regression test harness for streaming + long prompts.

sre-lead: creating incident ticket INC-20260314-42 and assigning follow-ups.

dylan: status (now): 5xx at 2.5%, canary stable 35m, promoting patch to 20% now. Will update when at 100% or if regressions seen.

ops-bot: :white_check_mark: Promotion to 20% completed. Rollout id=roll-20260314-002.

dylan: thanks team. If no regressions in next 40m we will re-enable batching on fallback first, then carefully on primary once at 100% patched. Postmortem target: created within 48h.

incident-bot: Incident state: mitigation in progress -> partial_mitigation. Severity: SEV2. Ticket: INC-20260314-42.

marie (oncall): left a note in pager duty handoff with link to this thread and the incident ticket. Good work everyone :thumbsup:

dylan: closing temporary routing in 2hr if stable. Will file RCA and notify customers.
